sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:131969
Court No. - 83
Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 1292 of 2024

Appellant :- X- Juvenile
Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Appellant :- Geetam Singh
Counsel for Respondent :- Ashutosh Gupta,G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Srivastava,J.

1. Supplementary affidavit preferred on behalf of the appellant after serving copy of the same upon
learned A.G.A. is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Geetam Singh, learned counsel for the appellant, Sri Ashutosh Gupta, learned counsel appearing on behalf of opposite party no.2 and learned A.G.A. for the State.
3.

This Criminal appeal under section 101(5) of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children)
Act, 2015 is directed against order dated 06.01.2024 passed by learned Special Judge, POCSO Act,
Kasganj in Bail Application No.2606 of 2023 (Ashu vs. State of U.P.) in connection with Case Crime X- Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42017531/
1 No. 114 of 2023 (S.C. No.1117 of 2023), under Sections 328, 376, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C., P.S. Amapur,
District- Kasganj, through which learned Special Judge rejected the aforesaid bail application.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that although the determination of the age of the appellant as drawn by learned trial court, is below the age of majority, but at the same time the psychological report, which has been taken into cognizance by learned concerned court itself demonstrates that appellant was having all ability to receive and respond as an adult, but at the same time learned counsel for the appellant also submitted that it is apparent from the record that the victim was having age of majority at the time of incident and she was having two children being the married lady.
5.

sentences.text: The incident narrated in the F.I.R. has been tallied with the statement recorded by the victim herself during trial and specifically in cross-examination dated 05.06.2024 through which it is crystal clear that the victim was aware and accompanied with the appellant with her own will and as such the appellant is co-operating with the trial court, but at the same time under incarceration only on the basis of F.I.R. and pendency of the trial is unjustified.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 vehemently opposed the prayer as made in the appeal and submitted that the order dated 06.01.2024 has been passed by learned court of Special Judge, POCSO Act, Kasganj on the basis of nature of the crime as well as the ability of juvenile, which has been assessed through psychological test that he was perfectly attain the ability as an adult to receive and to respond and his IQ level is 97.

7. Learned A.G.A. indicated certain cases as criminal history credited in favour of the appellant, but at the same time all the cases have been explained by learned counsel for the appellant, wherein three cases have been arising out of the same incident in which the appellant has been implicated and it is also apparent from the record that in retaliation all the three cases have been lodged against the appellant, whereas one F.I.R. has been lodged by the appellant also, which is related to the same village.
8.

After having the rival submissions extended by learned counsel for the parties, it is crystal clear that the statement recorded by victim herself, wherein she has been cross-examined on dated 05.06.2024, she submitted that she (victim) accompanied with the appellant along with her two children, who were dropped at the native village of her (victim) and thereafter she accompanied with the appellant to the place where the alleged crime has been committed.
9.
In view of the above facts and circumstances of the case, it is crystal clear that the victim was altogether aware that she has been accompanied with the appellant with her own will and wishes.
In these circumstances, learned Special Judge, POCSO Act, Kasganj was not justified in rejecting the bail application of appellant.
Thus, the impugned order is not sustainable and is liable to be set-aside.
10. Accordingly, the instant appeal is allowed.

The order impugned dated 06.01.2024 passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Kansganj in Bail Application No.2606 of 2023 is hereby X- Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42017531/
2 set-aside.
Order on Bail Application 11.

The appellant, X-Juvenile involved in Case Crime No. 114 of 2023 (S.C. No.1117 of 2023), under Sections 328, 376, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C., P.S. Amapur, District- Kasganj be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond through his natural guardian and two sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned.

Order Date :- 14.8.2024 Saif  X- Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42017531/
